title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 121
paragraphs: They, then, hard pressed as they were, carried out what had been ordered of them. From Acanthus Xerxes, after ordering the generals to wait for the fleet at Therma, let the ships sail apart from himself; (Therma is the city on the Thermaic gulf, which takes its name from it). He did this because he had been told that this was the shortest route. For from Doriscus as far as Acanthus the army had been marching thus: Xerxes had divided the whole land army into three divisions. One of them he assigned to march along the sea, accompanying the fleet; its commanders were Mardonius and Masistes. Another third of the army was ordered to march by the inland route, under the command of Tritantaechmes and Gergis. Meanwhile the third subdivision, with which Xerxes himself went, marched in the middle between them, under the command of Smerdomenes and Megabyzus.
